# How is writing different from speaking?

# Language in the World


---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_0.jpg)

# Ling Link



* We are all familiar with the Roman/Latin alphabet that we use to write English\!
  * Spend the next minute writing down the names of as many other writing systems as you can think of
  * Try to list the languages that are written using that writing system \(for example\, the Roman alphabet is used to write not only English but also Latin \[and all its daughter languages\]\, Germanic languages\, some Slavic languages\, in “Romanizations” of languages like Chinese\, Japanese\, etc\.\, and many more – about 70% of the written languages use it\!\)
  * If you don’t know the name of the writing system\, Google it\!
  * You can also jot down any interesting facts you know about the system

https://www.milestoneloc.com/latin-alphabet-usage-and-variations/

# Recall



* __Language acquisition __ is the process by which humans acquire the ability to use\, produce\, and perceive language\!
  * __First Language Acquisition: __ how an infant acquires his/her first or native language
  * __Second Language Acquisition: __ how children and adults acquire additional languages beyond the first
* Learning vs\. acquiring
* Critical period – need to acquire early\!
  * Interlanguage = stages on the way to acquiring fluency
  * Fossilization = hitting the wall of acquisition
* All languages are equally challenging; difficulty is relative

# Modes of linguistic communication


---


# Speech


---


# Signing

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_1.jpg)



* __Pros:__
  * Provides similar range as speaking for people who physically cannot speak
* __Cons:__
  * Requires use of hands
  * Must be viewed
  * Evaporates/cannot span time without the assistance of modern technology

---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_2.jpg)

# Writing



* __Pros:__
  * Pictographs \(we’ll later say this is NOT writing\) can be understood across languages
  * Can be read/understood more quickly than speaking can be heard/understood
  * Endures and has great reach
* __Cons:__
  * Takes longer to produce than speech
  * Requires use of hands
  * Must be viewed

---


# What is writing?

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_3.png)

__Writing__  allows humans to transmit information to others not within hearing distance\, both spatially and temporally

__Epic of Gilgamesh__


---


__Writing__  is the representation of language with the use of visual signs

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_4.png)

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_5.png)

__English Alphabet__


---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_6.png)

__\< Linguistics is awesome\. >__



* The primary goal of   __writing__  is to make our utterances\, which are by default audible\, visible

# Every writing system must represent language

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_7.tiff)

Represents the  _morpheme_   _pr _ ‘house’ & the  _syllable_  /pr/ in Egyptian

It’s  __iconic __ because the symbol looks like 	what it represents\!

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_8.tiff)

Represents the  _phonemes_  of Old Gaelic

It’s  __symbolic __ because there is 	no connection between the 	thing drawn and what it means


---


# Interactive



* Is the English alphabet  __iconic__  or  __symbolic__ ?
  * Symbolic

# The Cheyenne Indian Letter

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_9.jpg)



* 19th c\. message from Turtle\-Following\-His\-Wife to his son\, Little Man
  * Says something like: “Dad \(TFHW\) says to return home\, enclosed is $53 for the cost of the trip”
  * Is this “writing”? Why or why not?

---


# Pictographs ≠ writing!



* The Cheyenne letter is an instance of  __pictographs__
  * = picture writing
    * pictorial representation of objects\, ideas and events
  * Signs represent an event or an idea and not direct language
    * i\.e\.\, words\, morphemes\, phonemes\, etc\.
  * Independent of a word or utterance\, which refers to that object\, idea\, or event

---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_10.jpg)

# Speech vs. writing



  * Speech is continuous; writing is discrete

---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_11.png)



  * Speech is bound to utterance time; writing is not
  * Speech is temporary; writing is permanent


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_12.png)

__Tablet from Nippur\, 2000 __  __bce__


---


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_13.png)

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_14.png)



  * Speech is audible; writing is visible
  * Speech is produced by voice; writing is produced by hand
  * Diachrony\, not synchrony\, tends to be represented\.


![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_15.gif)

![](images/17-How%20is%20writing%20different%20from%20speaking_16.jpg)
